evidence.claim: Flagged txn 3509359 is $125.08, below the card's 180d mean of $218.79 (amount_z -0.24, 0.57x mean), far under the card max of $1,960.95.
Transaction is in the cardholder's only historical region 264 / country 87 (82 of 82 baseline txns), new_region_for_card = false.
Device 'Trident/7.0 | Windows 10 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080' is not in the card's 4 known devices and is flagged New for this account; no proxy recorded.
Product 'R' has 0% share in the 180d baseline (W 78, H 4) and online is only 4.9% of the card's channel mix, so the purchase type is out of profile.
No burst: only 1 online txn in the episode window; the other two window txns (3501882 $141.02, 3501890 $141.07) are in-person, in-region, and scored 0.10/0.11 — normal home activity continued.
No card-testing run and no just-under-$500 run detected; no rare shared devices and no cards linked by a rare device.
Region 264 shows 18 newcomer cards in 7d with a 0.39 fraud-history rate vs 0.10 base rate, but this card is not a newcomer (82 prior txns there), so the cluster does not implicate it.

Two prior confirmed account-takeover cases on the same card (CC-2277 $81.93, CC-2447 $33.95, Aug 2016) raise prior risk, but both involved small mixed-channel amounts reported by the cardholder, unlike this single mid-size in-region online purchase.
Closest semantic matches (CC-5236, CC-0099, CC-5224, CC-4395, CC-5142) are all high-scoring alerts on purchases from a device new to the account that the cardholder confirmed; all cleared.
Policy R1 requires verification rather than a block where probability is below 0.70 on a weak/ambiguous signal.
Customer confirms the $125.08 purchase from their new desktop; no other unrecognized activity reported.

case.summary: Case HHG-020 flags a $125.08 online purchase (txn 3509359) scored 0.52. The amount is below the card's own average, the region and country match the card's entire 180-day history, and in-person activity in region 264 continued on five days in the week around it. The adverse signals are limited to a device new to the account and a product code ('R') absent from the baseline — the classic ambiguous single online purchase, not the 2-4 transaction burst of card-not-present fraud. Two prior confirmed ATO cases on this card justified caution, but their signature (small mixed-channel items) does not repeat here, and there is no shared device or ring link. Verification was requested under R1; the cardholder confirmed the purchase, so the alert is cleared and the device should be added to the profile under R3.
